findings.title: Equal order values make provider selection nondeterministic
findings.body: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now sorts by CryptoProvider.order() reversed and picks index 0. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order()=200, so ties are broken only by ServiceLoader iteration order, which is classpath dependent. The old code failed fast on multiple providers; the new code can silently pick a different crypto implementation (e.g. FIPS vs non-FIPS) depending on classpath ordering.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider
findings.body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), i.e. whatever JCA provider supplies the default keystore type, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers using this as the BouncyCastle/BCFIPS provider (algorithm lookups, BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER assumptions) will get the wrong provider or null behavior, causing NoSuchAlgorithm/NoSuchProvider failures or wrong implementations.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks length validation
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature with len=signLength/2 and System.arraycopy without checking that signature.length==signLength or that signLength is even/positive. A short, long, or odd signLength causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException or silent truncation/padding, producing a corrupt DER signature instead of a clean IOException.

findings.title: Negative/oversized ECDSA integers silently truncated
findings.body: asn1derToConcatenatedRS decodes r/s as BigInteger without checking sign or range, and integerToBytes() silently keeps only the low qLength bytes when bytes.length>qLength. A crafted DER with negative or oversized integers is truncated into a valid-looking concatenated signature instead of rejected, hiding malformed input and enabling signature malleability issues.

findings.title: readSequence does not enforce exact DER length
findings.body: readSequence() loops while(length>0) subtracting each TLV's total size but never checks for length<0, trailing bytes after the sequence, or indefinite-length (-1) encoding. Overlong inner elements make length go negative and silently succeed, and indefinite length returns an empty list, so malformed signatures are accepted or reported with a misleading error.

findings.title: Most CryptoProvider operations throw UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, createECParams, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getX509CertFactory and others. When authz-client runs standalone (only this provider on the classpath, which CryptoIntegration.init now auto-selects), any code path needing signing, JWT client authentication, or cert handling fails at runtime. Plain-JCA defaults could be returned without BouncyCastle.

findings.title: Test reuses one EC key for all curves and never verifies
findings.body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key (typically P-256) and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512, then only asserts round-trip concatenated->DER->concatenated equality. It never verifies the signature with Signature.verify, so wrong signLength padding, truncation, or interop failures against real verifiers are not detected.
